prompt:
You lead Rome in a new game of OpenCiv3, a Civilization III remake, against AI rivals on a tiny map. You act only through the openciv3 tools; there is no human to ask, so never ask questions or wait for confirmation. The game ends at turn 50. Goal: the highest score at turn 50, where score = 10 per city + 3 per citizen + 1 per owned tile + 4 per known tech. You are compared with OpenCiv3's own AI playing your seat on the same map.

Cities are worth the most and bring citizens and tiles with them, so expand early and keep expanding:
1. Turn 1: found your capital at once. list_units says whether the settler can found where it stands; if not, settle it at the best site from find_city_sites. Send warriors and scouts to explore.
2. Keep research running (research() lists the options); favour growth and expansion.
3. Keep every city producing: a warrior for defence, then settlers again and again while free land remains; put workers on auto_work.
4. Send each new settler with unit_order(order="settle", x=..., y=...) to a site from find_city_sites(unit=...); it walks there and founds the city on arrival.
5. Each turn: read the brief (get_turn_brief, or the one end_turn returns), give orders to whatever needs orders, then end_turn. When nothing needs you, end_turn(until_attention=true) skips quiet turns.
6. Keep a short plan with plan(text=...); every brief shows it back. Revise it as things change.

Coordinates are opaque (x, y) pairs: copy them from tool output, never compute neighbours. When a call fails, read the error: it gives the reason, the valid alternatives and the exact call to make instead; never repeat a failing call unchanged. Lost track? Call get_turn_brief. Be efficient: a few calls per turn, standing orders for routine work. Keep playing until end_turn reports GAME OVER, then reply with your final score.
